summary.headline: NTPC reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore, up 12% YoY, and targets 150 GW by FY32 and 250 GW by FY37.
summary.overview: NTPC's 22nd Analysts and Institutional Investors Meet (held 27 July 2026, post Q1 results) centred on demand growth, the 250 GW FY37 capacity plan and INR 17 lakh crore capex envelope. Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 5,343 crore (up 12% YoY) and said FY26 standalone PAT was a record INR 23,162 crore. Renewable additions lagged target: 4.2 GW in FY26 and 1.9 GW added in FY27 to date, against a FY27 RE target of 7-8 GW. Technical-minimum and curtailment issues for thermal units, and a shift in the tender vs cost-plus debate, were the main analyst focus.

financial_highlights.change: Highest ever; FY22 INR 16,282 crore (9.21% CAGR)

financial_highlights.metric: Profit from JVs and subsidiaries FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 5.50 interim paid; INR 3.50 final recommended (about INR 9 total for FY26)

segments.name: Renewables (NTPC Green, NGEL)
segments.commentary: Operational RE capacity 12 GW; 4.2 GW added in FY26 and target of 7-8 GW in FY27 subject to transmission. NGEL generation about 15 BU vs 7 BU a year earlier. RE target 60 GW by FY32 and 136 GW by FY37.

segments.name: Coal and thermal
segments.commentary: Group coal capacity 66 GW at March 2026, planned to reach 77 GW, with 17 GW in pipeline (total 91 GW). Under-construction thermal around 16 GW. Sinnar 1,350 MW acquired with Mahagenco, first unit targeted this calendar year.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Target 30 GW by FY47 and about 6 GW by FY37. ASHVINI (NPCIL JV) building 2,800 MW at Mahi Banswara (PHWR); nuclear island EPC NIT floated 15 July 2026. Close to 34 sites under study.

segments.name: Storage and pumped storage
segments.commentary: Group BESS portfolio 38.9 GWh, with 6.62 GWh under execution (including 5 GWh co-located at thermal plants under regulated returns). Pumped storage: 1 GW Tehri operational, 13.2 GW allocated, 3-5 GW targeted by FY33.

segments.name: Mining (NTPC Mining Ltd)
segments.commentary: Production 47.8 million tonnes in Q1 (+8.5%), FY26 48.66 MT. Captive share of coal needs 18% now, targeted at 25% by FY30. Nine mines with 92 MTPA peak capacity.

segments.name: Green hydrogen and emerging
segments.commentary: Pudimadaka green hydrogen hub on 1,200 acres with about INR 1 lakh crore envisaged. Coal gasification (SNG) opportunity referenced in a INR 37,000 crore government scheme; NTPC says it is a serious contender.

guidance_outlook: Capacity target 150 GW by FY32 and 250 GW by FY37; fossil share of capacity to fall from 82% to 56% by FY32 and 39% by FY37.
Group capex about INR 1.08 lakh crore in FY26-27 (INR 56,000 crore spent in FY26), INR 5.97 lakh crore for FY28-32, and about INR 9.63 lakh crore for FY33-37; total about INR 17 lakh crore.
FY27 RE addition target of 7-8 GW, subject to transmission; management said 7 GW with storage is equivalent to roughly 8 GW of pure RE.
Dividend payout ratio to hover around 36-40%; management intends dividend to keep growing.
Generation share: RE to rise from 4% to about 33% of generation by FY37; total generation about 943 BU by FY37.
Sinnar unit commissioning targeted in calendar 2026; Pipalkoti pumped storage targeted for FY28 year-end, with a likely few-month slip.
capex_capacity: Group capacity about 127 GW, of which about 91 GW operational and 36 GW under construction; FY26 addition 9.6 GW, of which about 60% was RE. FY27 to date addition 1.9 GW.
Coal capacity 66 GW (March 2026), targeted 77 GW, with 17 GW in pipeline to reach 91 GW; beyond FY32 additions will depend on RE and demand.
Forced outage reduced to about 3.75% in FY26 from 3.9% the prior year and 4.1% earlier.
Pipeline: about 37 GW under construction and about 12 GW under tendering (per CMD). Group under-construction 35.7 GW (Investor presentation).
Coal gasification and BESS co-location at thermal plants are being developed; CO2 battery pilot expected to be commissioned by October-November 2026.
demand_pricing: Peak demand crossed 270 GW (record 271 GW in May 2026), with a projected 450+ GW by FY36 per CMD.
Management said year-to-date all-India energy met rose 9.28%, and NTPC generation about 8% YTD; NTPC rail-fed stations up 18% YTD.
PLF about 77% after backing down; management says this is despite must-run RE.
Curtailment and technical minimum (55% for coal units) are pressuring thermal units; the regulator now allows units below 55% to shut down and restart after about a day.

Regulated return: post-commissioning around 15.5% pre-tax equivalent to 12-13% returns, per CMD. Management prefers cost-plus brownfield over competitive bidding, citing equity scarcity and sustainability of returns.
Management cited a cost of debt of 5.89% (per analyst), a figure management did not dispute.

qa_highlights.question: Can NTPC accelerate RE additions, given FY26 missed target and FY27 target of 7 GW vs about 0.6 GW delivered?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said RE should not be measured in MW alone; storage is needed, and 7 GW with storage is equivalent to about 8 GW. Transmission delays are a key constraint.

qa_highlights.question: How does NTPC plan to handle thermal units falling below technical minimum during peak solar hours?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a regulatory change allowing shutdown below 55% with capacity charges still recovered, co-located BESS of 5 GWh at thermal plants, and advocacy for uniform technical minimum. Smaller flexible units are being designed for cycling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for coal capacity and FY32-37 RE additions?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal capacity to reach 77 GW by FY32 and 91 GW with pipeline; beyond that, additions depend on RE and demand. Nuclear to reach about 6 GW by FY37.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend payout policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Director (Finance) said payout will hover around 36-40%, with dividend trend maintained through FY37.

qa_highlights.question: Why are states preferring tendered coal capacity over regulated cost-plus projects, and why is NTPC not bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: CMD said NTPC focuses on brownfield cost-plus projects with PPAs for healthy and transparent returns. Director (Finance) cited limited equity capacity and stated that competitive bids would compress margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will NTPC add coal gasification and nuclear capacity, and is there a plan for smaller flexible thermal units?
qa_highlights.answer: Coal gasification (SNG) is a significant opportunity; NTPC considers itself a serious contender for the INR 37,000 crore scheme. Smaller flexible units could amount to tens of GW, to be located at load centres and designed for fast start and stop, pending regulatory approval.

risks_watch: RE execution lag: 4.2 GW added in FY26 and only 1.9 GW in FY27 to date against a 7-8 GW target, constrained by transmission availability.
Curtailment and technical minimum: rising backing down of coal units could raise costs and pressure returns, which management says it will protect through policy advocacy.
Capex envelope of about INR 17 lakh crore to FY37 needs sustained funding; equity availability is a stated constraint on competitive bids.
Nuclear execution: first EPC package NIT floated July 2026; sites and JV partners still being finalised.
Hydrogen commercial viability is far off per management; coal gasification and CO2 battery timelines (Oct-Nov 2026) need monitoring.
Pipalkoti pumped storage may slip a few months past FY28 year-end.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, long-term capex and financial strength, but defensive on RE delivery and curtailment; management answered several questions by redirecting to storage and policy advocacy. Evasive on specific tender participation and on the reasons for not bidding in competitive auctions.
key_quotes: Outstanding receivable days improved to 15 days from 31 days.
So, if it is about an one hour or two hours, it is better to curtail the renewable rather than stopping the thermal plant because in the evening you will be left without power.
And one per megawatt hour is roughly about INR1 crore plus on that side.
There is no plant which we are undertaking which is without PPA.

Coal capacity from 66 GW to 77 GW target, with 17 GW pipeline (to 91 GW)
Sinnar 1,350 MW thermal unit (with Mahagenco), first unit targeted calendar 2026
ASHVINI 2,800 MW PHWR nuclear at Mahi Banswara; nuclear island EPC NIT floated 15 July 2026

growth.why: Management targets 7-8 GW RE additions in FY27 (only 1.9 GW added so far, and FY26 RE additions of 0.6-4.2 GW lagged target), a 150 GW portfolio by FY32 backed by ~36 GW under construction and ~12 GW under tendering, and group capex of ~INR 17 lakh crore to FY37; quarterly revenue and EBITDA growth were not given (PAT +12% YoY reported, not revenue/EBITDA).
